title: What Do You Think?
subtitle: Four ways to ask for and give an opinion
review: Notes and questions written by Claude: check the English lines, the notes and the questions. No Burmese yet.
intro: A painting that may be upside down, a soup with something missing, two movies to choose from and a brand-new mustache: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they ask for an opinion, how they give one, and the polite words they use when they don't like something.

lines.note: Hung is the past of hang: put something on a wall.
What do you think? asks for someone's opinion.
Honestly? = do you want the true answer?
I think… gives your opinion. The pause before interesting means: I don't really like it.
A compliment: nice words about someone or something.

lines.text: In my opinion, it's upside down.
lines.note: In my opinion = I think. Upside down: the top is at the bottom.

lines.text: No, it isn't. It's abstract art.
lines.note: Abstract art shows shapes and colors, not real things.

lines.text: Lucas, the signature is at the top.
lines.note: The signature is the painter's name. It is usually at the bottom.

lines.text: So, how do you like my soup?
lines.note: How do you like…? asks for an opinion about something you made or bought.
Different, after a pause, is a polite way to say you don't like it.

lines.text: I feel like something is missing.
lines.note: I feel like + a sentence = I think so, but I'm not sure. Missing: not there.
I don't think so: a soft no.
I'm not sure: you don't have a clear opinion.

lines.text: So what's missing, in your opinion?
lines.note: In your opinion? asks what the other person thinks.

lines.text: The phone number of the pizza place.
lines.note: He would rather order a pizza.

lines.text: There are two movies. Which one is better, in your opinion?
lines.note: Which one…? asks you to choose between things.
No question = I am completely sure.

lines.text: Absolutely. If you ask me, it's a masterpiece.
lines.note: Absolutely: a strong yes. If you ask me = in my opinion. A masterpiece: a very great work.

lines.text: Perfect. We'll watch the second one.
What? But you asked for my opinion!
lines.note: Ask for someone's opinion: ask what they think.

lines.text: I did. So I'd know which one to avoid.
lines.note: I did = yes, I asked. Avoid: stay away from. She doesn't like the movies he likes.

lines.text: So? What do you think of my mustache?
lines.note: What do you think of + a thing? asks for an opinion. A mustache: hair above the lip.
Brave usually means not afraid. Here it is a polite way to say: that was a risky choice.

lines.text: Personally, I think it makes me look serious.
lines.note: Personally = for me. It makes me look serious: people see me as serious.

lines.text: Do you want my honest opinion?
lines.note: Ask this before you say something the other person may not like.

lines.text: It makes you look like your uncle Gerald.
lines.note: Look like: seem the same as another person.

lines.text: So do I. But I didn't marry him.
lines.note: So do I = me too.

notes: Asking for an opinion: What do you think? What do you think of…? How do you like…? Which one is better, in your opinion?
Giving your opinion: I think…, In my opinion…, If you ask me…, Personally, I think…, I feel like…
Not sure: Maybe. I'm not sure. I don't think so.
Before a hard truth: Honestly? Do you want my honest opinion?
Interesting, different and brave can be polite words for 'I don't like it'. The pause before them says the rest.

questions.q: Lucas wants Emma's opinion of the painting. What does he ask?
questions.why: What do you think? asks for an opinion. How do you think? is not correct English.

questions.q: Why does Emma think the painting is upside down?
options: The signature is at the top.
questions.why: A painter's signature is usually at the bottom.

questions.q: Lucas is not sure about the pepper. What does he say?
questions.why: No question and absolutely mean you are completely sure.

questions.q: Which phrase means the same as 'in my opinion'?
questions.why: If you ask me, it's a masterpiece = in my opinion, it's a masterpiece.

questions.q: Why does Emma ask Lucas which movie is better?
options: To know which one to avoid
questions.why: I did. So I'd know which one to avoid.

questions.q: Emma says the mustache is brave. What does she really mean?
options: She thinks it was a risky choice.
She thinks Lucas is not afraid.
questions.why: Brave is a polite word here. Then she says it makes him look like his uncle.
